observations:
After reading the full source text of LM2 Torah 44 and examining all edges in the dataset (zero bechina edges, one eitza edge for reference 1044), the two packages identified — Package 1 (אמונה/תמימות/לב, good) and Package 2 (כפירה/אפיקורסות/חקירה, evil) — account for all the conceptual content of this Torah organized by bechina language.

The Torah is short and structurally simple. It advances a single argument with one central bechina at its core (faith = spoken faith = tamimut = lev) and one evil counterpart (kefira = apikorset = chakira = dimyonot). There is no third independent domain.

The remaining concepts that appear in the Torah but are NOT part of a bechina cluster:

1. מרה שחורה / חיות — Melancholy and vitality (para 5). The Rebbe says the overly scrupulous have no חיות because of their דקדוקים. This is an eitza relationship (scrupulousness → lack of vitality), not a bechina cluster. Chiyut is not equated with emunah here — it is its fruit. This cannot form a third package because: (a) there is no 'בְּחִינַת' language applied to it, and (b) only two concepts are involved (chiyut and mara shchora), which is insufficient for an independent domain of 3+.

2. אבות הקדושים / מסורת (holy forefathers / received tradition) — Mentioned in para 3 as the source of emunah: 'דַּי לָנוּ בֶּאֱמוּנָתֵנוּ שֶׁקִּבַּלְנוּ מֵאֲבוֹתֵינוּ הַקְּדוֹשִׁים'. This is an eitza relationship (the forefathers transmitted emunah), not a separate domain. The forefathers are not called a 'bechina' of emunah — they are its historical source.

3. חומרות יתרות / דקדוקים (excessive stringencies / over-scrupulousness) — Eitza: they lead to mara shchora. Not called a bechina of anything. Part of the negative domain but a behavioral category rather than a conceptual bechina family.

Conclusion: Torah 44 is organized around a single axis — the polarity of simple faith vs. corrupting inquiry — with one good package and one evil package. No third conceptual domain with 3+ bechina-connected nodes exists in this text.
